## Pull request overview

This PR aims to close out ROADMAP P1–P4 items by improving schema typing (Zod discriminated unions), expanding scaffolding and Storybook coverage, adding focus-management hooks and shared view skeleton/state primitives, and publishing new documentation pages.

**Changes:**
- Switched multiple `@object-ui/types` Zod schema unions to `z.discriminatedUnion('type', ...)` for better TS narrowing/autocomplete.
- Added new runtime primitives (focus-management hooks; shared skeleton/state components) and expanded Storybook stories across plugin packages.
- Updated CLI `init` scaffolding to generate a Vite + Tailwind project, and added new docs sections/pages (Guide deployment + API schema reference) plus ROADMAP status updates.

### Reviewed changes

`useFocusReturn` sets up the unmount cleanup effect with an empty dependency array. If `enabled` or `restoreOnUnmount` is false on the initial render and becomes true later, the cleanup will never be registered, so focus won't be restored on unmount. Consider including `enabled`/`restoreOnUnmount` in the effect deps (or always register the cleanup and check flags inside it) so toggling these options behaves correctly.

The generated `src/index.css` only contains `@import 'tailwindcss';`. In this repo, the design tokens/utilities (e.g., `bg-background`, CSS variables, `@theme`, and `tailwindcss-animate`) are defined in the app CSS (see `apps/console/src/index.css` / `packages/components/src/index.css`). Without those tokens, the scaffolded app will miss expected ObjectUI styling. Consider generating a fuller `index.css` (copy the base theme block) or documenting/importing the required token definitions.

The `PageSchema` example uses `"pageType": "detail"`, but `PageType` in `@object-ui/types` is `'record' | 'home' | 'app' | 'utility'`. Also, `regions` uses `body`, but the schema uses `components` for region content. Please update the example JSON to match the actual types so readers can copy/paste successfully.

New hooks (`useFocusReturn`, `useRovingFocus`) add non-trivial focus/keyboard behavior, but there are no accompanying tests. `packages/react/src/__tests__` already covers other hooks (e.g. `useNavigationOverlay`, `usePageTransition`), so it would be good to add a focused test file (e.g. verify restoration when `enabled` toggles and arrow-key roving across items).

`ViewSkeleton`'s switch statement has no default/fallback return. If an unexpected `variant` value is passed (or the union widens), this component returns `undefined`, which React will treat differently than `null` and can be confusing. Return `null` (or add an exhaustive check) as a safe fallback.
```suggestion
      return <ChartSkeleton {...props} />
    default: {
      const _exhaustiveCheck: never = variant
      return null
    }
```

The Dockerfile snippet pins `pnpm@9`, but the repo’s `packageManager` is `pnpm@10.28.2`. Using a different major pnpm version can cause lockfile/install differences. Consider updating the docs to match the repo’s packageManager version (or describe the supported range explicitly).
```suggestion
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10.28.2 --activate
```

The Netlify example sets `PNPM_VERSION = "9"`, which conflicts with the repo’s `packageManager` (`pnpm@10.28.2`). Consider updating this to the same pnpm major (or explaining why v9 is required).
```suggestion
  PNPM_VERSION = "10"
```

This `pageType` description lists values like `"list"`, `"detail"`, etc., but `PageType` is currently `'record' | 'home' | 'app' | 'utility'` (see `packages/types/src/layout.ts`). Please align the documented `PageType` values with the actual exported type.

This story is under `plugin-calendar`, but the schema uses `type: 'object-grid'` with `viewType: 'calendar'`, which exercises the grid view-switching path rather than the calendar renderer directly. Consider using `type: 'object-calendar'` or `type: 'calendar'` here to showcase the calendar plugin itself (and reduce cross-plugin coupling in Storybook).
```suggestion
    type: 'object-calendar',
    objectName: 'Event',
    calendar: {
      startDateField: 'startDate',
      endDateField: 'endDate',
      titleField: 'title',
    },
```
